newsitem.title: USA: NZ SPORT -Disappointment for Nobilo at Winged Foot.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT -Disappointment for Nobilo at Winged Foot.

text.p: MAMARONECK, New York, Aug 17 - The closest New Zealander Frank Nobilo came to the United States PGA Championship trophy was late Sunday afternoon (US time) when he walked from the recorder's room at the Winged Foot Golf Club for the last time.
The handsome Rodman Wanamaker trophy stood on a table two metres from where the final 79 players in the 79th United States PGA, sat to sign their scorecards.
Nobilo was in no mood for a fireside chat as he exited the room, dodging waiting reporters as he quickly went into the nearby men's locker room.
Nobilo shot a disappointing four-over 74 today, after making a bright start to at one point be within eight shots of eventual champion Davis Love 3.
He emerged 30 minutes later, showered and changed, with the outcome of the PGA Championship all but sealed.
Love led young Justin Leonard by three shots, with three holes to play. The quietly-spoken South Carolina native eventually won by five shots.
As disappointed as he was, Nobilo can take enormous pride in his performance in golf's four majors this year.

Unlike some of the world's leading players, Nobilo managed to make the halfway cut in all four majors, finishing 46th in April's United States Masters, tied-36th in the United States Open, tied-10th in last month's British Open, and now tied-29th in the United States PGA.
He's now extended his run of four-round results in the majors to eight.

Since 1986, when the Aucklander contested his first British Open, Nobilo has appeared in 21 majors, and managed to make the cut in an impressive 17. His British Open record in particular stands at nine appearances, nine finishes.
Likewise, he has a 100 percent record in the United States Open, finishing in the money in all four he's entered, capped by an excellent tied-ninth finish at Oakmont in 1994.
He missed the cut in his first Masters appearance in 1995 but demonstrated his enormous talent capturing a resounding fourth place result a year later, behind Britain's Nick Faldo.
Five results in six appearances in United States PGA events too is indicative of Nobilo's highly respected status among his peers.

The Winged Foot course, venue for this year's PGA, was always going to win out in the end, even though Love finished 11-under. The course never let up allowing just four players from a starting field of 150, to break par after four torrid rounds.
Nobilo arrived last Monday at the front gate of the Winged Foot Golf Club full of optimism.

And though he left six days later full of disappointment, there is, after Love's victory, the comfort that the list of players who wear the 'Best Players Not to Win a Major' tag now has Nobilo moving ahead one place closer to golf's ultimate
